newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fuji Bank to help struggling construction firm.
newsitem.headline: Fuji Bank to help struggling construction firm.

text.p: Fuji Bank Ltd said on Friday that it would give full support to struggling construction company Tobishima Corp, which is suffering under the weight of huge debts.
"We will extend full support to Tobishima," a senior bank official told a news conference.

Tobishima has fallen into hard financial times due to aggressive borrowing for its property-related business during the so-called "bubble" era of inflated asset prices in the late 1980s. It was not able to keep up with loan repayments after the bubble burst in the early 1990s.

In October, it drew up a restructuring programme to try to solve its problems and asked its creditors to reduce their claims against it for debts owed by its group firms to 100 billion yen ($900 million) from about 740 billion yen ($6.66 billion).
Fuji Bank is one of Tobishima's major creditors, which number 50.
"We are now asking financial institutions for support," Tobishima said in a statement on Friday.

Tobishima said when it announced the restructuring plan that it and its group companies owed a total of 1.09 trillion yen ($9.8 billion). Of the total, the parent company's debts totalled 190 billion yen ($1.71 billion), while the group companies owed the rest, it said.
Of the 900 billion yen ($8.10 billion) owed by the group companies, 740 billion yen ($6.66 billion) had been guaranteed by Tobishima, it said.
The rest was not guaranteed, and the group companies will continue to be held responsible for repayment under the new plan, Tobishima said.
Both Tobishima and Fuji Bank on Friday announced their earnings for the six months to September 30.
Despite the financial difficulties, Tobishima posted a parent current profit of 1.76 billion yen ($15.8 million), up 20.9 percent from the same period a year ago.

It maintained its forecast for a parent current profit in the full 1996/97 business year at 8.5 billion yen ($76.5 million), which is slightly larger than its actual profit of 8.4 billion yen ($75.6 million) in the year earlier period.
"We think we can achieve our initial target by trying very hard to get orders and through our cost-cutting efforts," the company said.

Fuji Bank, which itself has been hurt by aggressive lending to property-related businesses in the late 1980s, said its first-half parent current profit soared 207 percent to 57.39 billion yen ($517 million) from the year-ago period.
The bank said it would post a parent current profit of 70 billion yen ($630 million) in 1996/97, against a loss of 500.09 billion yen ($4.50 billion) in the year-ago period.
